literal: Without thinking, 'They have rare self-control, indeed they are pitiable,' love, transgressing secrecy, will appear in the public place.
translation: Without considering, 'These people have rare self-control,' or 'They deserve pity,' love overflows its secrets and exposes itself in public.
modern: இவர்கள் மிகுந்த மனவலிமை உடையவர்கள் என்றும், இவர்கள் இரங்கத்தக்கவர்கள் என்றும் எண்ணாமல், காமமானது தன் இரகசியங்களைக் கடந்து பொதுவெளியில் வெளிப்பட்டுவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet describes how overwhelming passion cannot be hidden by modesty or self-restraint. The speaker notes that love (kāmam) does not pause to think whether the lovers possess rare self-control (niṟai) or whether they deserve pity (aḷiyar) for their suffering. Instead, it breaks through all barriers of privacy and secrecy (maṟai) and reveals itself openly in public (maṉṟu). The contrast between internal restraint and the unstoppable public manifestation of love highlights the helplessness of the lovers.
